lead.title: Philips agrees to pay €288M to the US DoJ to settle the Respironics recall case
lead.deck: The agreement in principle covers the Department of Justice proceedings over the June 2021 recall of CPAP/BiPAP devices and ventilators (polyurethane foam fault, about 15 million units). Payment is expected in Q1 2027; the state attorneys general probe remains open, while Philips reiterates 2026 guidance (+3 to 4.5% comparable sales) after €4.4B of Q3 sales.

milestone.title: GE HealthCare adds AI-powered AutoAS and Lung Guidance to its Vscan Air handheld ultrasound, both CE-marked and FDA-cleared
milestone.summary: AutoAS visually estimates moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis from standard 2D views (with a confidence score); Lung Guidance gives real-time directions across the 8-zone lung protocol and auto-captures clips. In validation tests, non-expert users obtained diagnostic-quality lung scans in 95.2% of evaluations versus 96.8% for experts.
milestone.why: On-device AI in handheld ultrasound cuts operator dependence and extends cardiopulmonary screening beyond the cardiologist: one to watch for imaging-AI startups, whose distribution runs through such platforms. Rollout by late November 2026 via Innovation Packages.

brefsIntl.title: Zimmer Biomet raises 2026 guidance after a Q3 above $2B (+3.1%), helped by THINK Surgical robotics
brefsIntl.summary: The technology, data, bone cement and surgical segment grew 11.9% ($180.6M); the expanded THINK Surgical agreement gives Zimmer exclusive distribution of the TMINI handheld robot. Growth guidance raised to 4.4–4.9%.

word.fr: Continuous glucose measurement with no needle or subcutaneous sensor
word.definition: Tracking blood glucose continuously with no needle or filament under the skin, using optical or radio-frequency signals read through the skin.

parts.label: Emitter
parts.role: sends an infrared or microwave signal into the skin

parts.label: Receiver
parts.role: picks up the response altered by glucose

parts.label: Algorithm
parts.role: turns the raw signal into a glucose value

how.t: A mid-infrared laser (DiaMonTech) or an RF/microwave signal (Afon) probes the tissue at the skin or wrist.
Glucose absorbs or alters the signal in a measurable way; the sensor records it.
A calibrated model converts the measurement into a glucose value; accuracy remains the clinical bottleneck (Afon: ~75% normal/elevated classification in a first real-world trial).

word.why: Invasive CGMs (Dexcom G7 15 Day, +11% Q3 sales) opened a multi-billion-dollar market; non-invasive is the moonshot: no cleared product among the players cited, so high technical risk but huge value if accuracy reaches CGM standard.

startups.name: Afon Technology
startups.use: Glucowear, an RF/microwave wrist sensor; ~75% classification accuracy (normal/elevated) in a first real-world trial presented at ATTD 2026; manufacturing planned with Sony UK Technology Centre

startups.name: DiaMonTech
startups.use: D-Pocket, glucose measurement by mid-infrared laser; reported MARD of 19.6–20.7% (company data), still in development; Samsung Ventures on the cap table

startups.name: Indigo Diabetes
startups.use: Implantable subcutaneous sensor (evanescent field) measuring glucose, ketones and lactate; GLOW and then 6-month SHINE feasibility studies run
